full_query: Will the antibiotics prevent the lyme disease from progressing?
sentences: Antibiotics are effective in treating Lyme disease, particularly in its early stages
The primary goal of antibiotic treatment is to eliminate the infection caused by Borrelia burgdorferi, the bacterium responsible for Lyme disease
In the early stages of Lyme disease, antibiotics such as doxycycline or amoxicillin are commonly prescribed to prevent the progression of the disease
These antibiotics work by targeting the bacteria and preventing them from reproducing and spreading
However, if left untreated, Lyme disease can progress to its later stages, which may involve more severe symptoms such as arthritis, neurological problems, and heart issues
In these cases, treatment may involve longer courses of antibiotics or additional medications to manage symptoms

It is essential to note that antibiotics are not effective against the late-stage symptoms of Lyme disease, such as arthritis or neurological problems, which are thought to be caused by the body's immune response to the infection rather than the bacteria itself
In these cases, treatment focuses on managing symptoms and alleviating discomfort
